source_text: Hm... I do like reading things based on HEAD but keeping in mind HEAD is like from jazz or free jazz... it won't tell us whether the mission has spun off into abstractions like M-wyrd-modernism or returned from abstractions to something quite concrete like M-the-perfect-crime.  I think in addition to the HEAD we might want something a little bit like a chord "cheat sheet", like a very quick distillation of the scopes and keywords from across the mission.

reply_text:
㊥ (gist) Added as B1d (futon2 `ff22a2876`), queued for codex-33 right after B1c: a one-line cheat sheet per item, computed from the whole document and its history rather than HEAD. The part of your remark that does the most work for the outer cascade is *register and its direction* — concrete vs abstract, and whether the mission is heading out or coming back — because that is the feasibility signal B2 could not get from commit history (4 of 107 had any), and it is exactly what HEAD alone cannot show.

㊭ (the sheet) Five fields, all classical counts so the sheet is the same on every run: *scopes* — repos and directories its paths touch, by count; *keywords* — tf-idf over the 107 plus any declared ones; *the changes* — the applied patterns in order of first mention, the progression under the tune; *register* — per section, the share of lines carrying a path, sha, number, checkbox or date against prose lines, with its trajectory early→late and first commits→last, so "spun off into abstraction" and "returned to something concrete" read as a direction; and the status line. One line: `| scope futon3c/agency ×41 · futon2/aif ×12 | keys clock, lineage, dispatch | changes p1 → p2 → p3 | register 0.62 ↑ |`. Worked examples are your two: `M-weird-modernism` (1,037 lines, 101 paths, 5 checkboxes, "perpetual-projection mode — no closure phase scheduled") and `M-the-perfect-crime` (557 lines, 100 paths, 6 checkboxes, 13 commit shas). Acceptance is that those two read right to you.

🈖 (where it enters the cascade) The `observe` square today emits an item as id, kind, source pin and one locator. The sheet is what it should emit instead — the item as a chord chart, not a bar — and register/trajectory become the token the feasibility square consumes, where B2's commit share would have gone. In §5a's terms it is Crumb's panel sequence compressed to a line beside the current panel.

㊢ (in flight) B1c (revealed attention and co-work) running on codex-33, job `invoke-1791243893154-33311-1ff8ab13`, park `park-e97cad31`; B1d follows; B3 then has B1–B2 and the sheet to draw on.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (gist) Taken as guidance rather than as a defect in the data: if `unblocks` was never written down, B1b will mostly confirm that, and the first cut comes from behaviour. I added B1c to the excursion (futon2 `55c39bb0c`) — revealed attention and co-work, from records that already exist — and recorded your enabler/blocker distinction and the "subject to constraints" point as the frame for B3. codex-33 is still on B1b (its report and script are sitting untracked in the tree, not yet committed); B1c follows it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("we can infer … from the fact that I'm working on E-aif-cascade right now") The records for that inference are already in Cascade Live, just not read as such: `:lineage` is 126 dispatch records `{agent target session at dispatched-by}` — the very field B1 had to set aside because it is not predecessor/successor — and its top targets today are `diagramprover` 25, `apm-demonstration` 22, `the-perfect-crime` 14, `convert-operator-turns-to-patterns` 7, `象-2000` 6; the first lineage row is this excursion, dispatched by me to codex-33 an hour ago. The operator side is the turn store's "mission the operator was working under" (the `turn-traced` view). B1c reads both per item, keeps them apart, and reports ρ against the occurrence count and against B1's coupling measure.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("not a 'blocker' but an enabler") That is a different relation again, and B1c names it so: *co-work* — items targeted by one session, by one agent within a day, or named together in one operator turn — is undirected and says "these are worked together", which is your diagramprover-with-Lean-and-cascades case; `unblocks` is directed and says "this must advance for that to"; coupling through shared patterns (B1) is a third. The proposal in B1c is that attention becomes the `unblocks` token's first-cut value as an *enabler weight*, superseded by a declaration wherever one exists, and never called a dependency.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("a deep-dive to fully plan all of the work across all time is actually not a good use of time") Agreed, and it is already the shape of the machinery: G is scored to a horizon (R13), the field is whatever HEAD holds, and §5a has the outer cascade refined as runs return rather than specified in advance. B3 will be written as the first cut — the squares as they can be filled today, typed absences where they cannot — not as the rigorous dependency study.
